name: CLASS B AUTOCLAVE
desc: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS INNO-AU-B-220 Class B Autoclave is a highly efficient, fully automatic benchtop steam sterilizer designed to meet strict EN13060 European standards for the reliable decontamination of medical and dental instruments. Ideal for dental clinics and surgical research labs to sterilize wrapped, porous, and hollow instruments.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS Class B Autoclave is a fully automatic, microprocessor-controlled, vacuum-assisted steam sterilizer that meets EN13060 for terminal sterilization of wrapped, porous, hollow, and solid loads. It uses a built-in steam generator to produce saturated steam and a high-capacity vacuum pump to perform pre-vacuum and post-vacuum fractionated air removal, ensuring deep steam penetration into complex dental handpieces, surgical instruments, culture media, and laboratory glassware. Doctors and dental clinicians use it to sterilize stainless steel scalpels, forceps, scissors, dental handpieces, and endodontic files under ISO 17665 and EN13060 standards. B.Sc. and M.Sc. students use it to prepare sterile nutrient agar, potato dextrose agar, Luria-Bertani broth, phosphate-buffered saline, and reusable petri dishes for culturing Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, Bacillus subtilis, and Saccharomyces cerevisiae. PhD researchers and chemists autoclave microcentrifuge tubes, pipette tips, membrane filters, and biological assay reagents, and decontaminate spent cultures or biohazard waste containing Geobacillus stearothermophilus spores and genetically modified bacteria before disposal. At 121°C/134°C and a maximum working pressure of 240 kPa, saturated steam denatures enzymes, nucleic acids, and structural proteins of microorganisms, while post-vacuum drying removes residual moisture and Bowie-Dick, Helix, and vacuum tests verify air removal, steam penetration, and chamber leak-tightness. This autoclave is not intended for strong acids, volatile organic solvents, flammable liquids, or sealed containers, which must never be placed inside the chamber.
sop: Place the autoclave on a stable bench and check that the clean water tank contains distilled or deionized water up to the 4 L mark and the waste water collection tank is empty.
Connect the unit to a 220 V, 50 Hz grounded electrical supply and switch ON the main power; confirm the LED display and built-in mini printer initialize.

Load the three stainless steel wire mesh trays with cleaned, wrapped, pouched, or loose instruments; do not overload and keep space between items for steam penetration, especially for hollow and porous loads.
Close and latch the chamber door firmly; verify the double safety door lock engages and the high-temperature silicone rubber gasket seals the chamber.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target parameter, such as 121°C for heat-sensitive media or 134°C for wrapped surgical instruments and drying time between 1 and 60 minutes.
Press 'SET' again to lock the value.
Select the appropriate preselected program with the soft push buttons, for example wrapped, unwrapped, porous, hollow, or Bowie-Dick/Helix/Vacuum test, and confirm on the LED display.

Press START to begin the cycle; the high-capacity vacuum pump will perform pre-vacuum pulses, the built-in steam generator will generate saturated steam, and the chamber will pressurize to a maximum of 240 kPa.
Wait until the sterilization and post-vacuum drying programs are complete, the pressure gauge reads zero, the door lock releases automatically, and the built-in printer records the cycle parameters.
Wearing heat-resistant gloves, open the door slowly, stand clear of escaping steam, and remove the trays with a tray handler; allow sterilized items to cool before use or storage.
For daily validation, run a Bowie-Dick or Helix test cycle with the appropriate test pack and review the printed report for evidence of adequate air removal and steam penetration.
After daily use, switch OFF the unit, drain the waste water collection tank, rinse the clean water tank if required, log the cycle data, and leave the chamber door slightly ajar.

CRITICAL SAFETY WARNING: Never autoclave sealed containers, flammable liquids, volatile organic solvents, strong acids, chlorinated solutions, or toxic chemicals; never attempt to open the door during a cycle or force the lock, as this may cause severe steam burns, explosion, or instrument damage. Always wear heat-resistant gloves and safety goggles, and verify zero chamber pressure before opening.
